description: Published records of four real lunar landers and the checks the core must pass against them. Every published value was read from its source on 14 November 2026 and is given as printed, with the wording that shows its precision. Committed before the core was run on these cases.

sp4029_landing.title: NASA SP-2000-4029, Apollo by the Numbers: table 'LM Lunar Landing'
sp4029_landing.note: Coordinates footnote: IAU Mean Earth Polar Axis coordinate system. The row 'Sun Angle (deg)' has no definition on the page.

sp4029_windows.title: NASA SP-2000-4029, Apollo by the Numbers: table 'Launch Windows'
sp4029_windows.note: Row 'Targeted Lunar Sun Elevation Angle (deg)': Apollo 11 10.8, Apollo 16 11.9. These are the same numbers as the 'Sun Angle' row of the landing table, so that row is read as the targeted angle.

sp4029_apollo16.title: NASA SP-2000-4029, Apollo by the Numbers: Apollo 16 summary
sp4029_apollo16.note: Landing 'at 02:23:35 GMT on 21 April ... at 104:29:35'; the LM 'remained in lunar orbit six hours longer than planned'.

alsj_altaz.title: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal: Sun and Earth altitude and azimuth table (Scotti_AltAz.txt)
alsj_altaz.note: Header: times in UT; sub-Earth and sub-solar points interpolated from the Nautical Almanac lunar ephemeris; altitude and azimuth derived from them; landing times from 'Apollo by the Numbers'. Values printed to 0.01 degree. The table states the site coordinates it used, which differ slightly from the actual landing coordinates.

alsj_sunangles.title: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal: 'Sun Angles', compiled by Brian W. Lawrence, last revised 8 February 1999
alsj_sunangles.note: Apollo 16 landing 104.50 GET; 'Apollo 16 (as planned)' landing 98.75 GET; 'delayed by a bit less than 6 hours'.

lroc_blue_ghost.title: LROC: 'Blue Ghost Lunar Lander Seen From Above', 7 March 2025
lroc_blue_ghost.note: The page does not name the reference frame of the coordinates; LROC products use the mean-Earth/polar-axis frame (unverified for this page).

lroc_chandrayaan3.note: The page does not name the reference frame of the coordinates (unverified, as above).

cases.mission: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1, Mare Crisium, landed 2 March 2025; end of the lunar day on 16 March 2025
cases.terrain: none: no elevation data for this latitude in the project's terrain set. Smooth local sphere through the landing point (1737.4 km minus 3.65 km), observer 2 m above it.

published.note: CST is UTC-6; US daylight saving time began on 9 March 2025.

published.as_printed: more than 14 days of surface operations (346 hours of daylight)
imagery of the lunar sunset on March 16
published.precision: 1 day; the release uses US Central Daylight Time (UTC-5)

published.as_printed: final data received around 6:15 pm CDT on March 16
operating just over 5 hours into the lunar night

checks.computed: last light (upper limb of the Sun on the smooth local sphere, seen from 2 m) must fall between 2025-03-16T05:00:00 and 2025-03-17T05:00:00 UTC

checks.published: landing_time plus daylight_hours = 2025-03-16T18:34 UTC, taken as early as rounding allows: 18:04 UTC
checks.computed: last light as above must not be earlier than 2025-03-16T18:04:00 UTC

checks.published: landing_time plus daylight_hours (18:34 UTC); final_data minus night_operation (before 18:15 UTC)
checks.computed: times at which the lower limb, the centre and the upper limb of the Sun reach the smooth local horizon; elevation of the Sun's upper limb at 18:34 UTC (the height of the local horizon that would explain the difference)
checks.why_not_judged: The operational end of daylight depends on local terrain, which is not in the project's data for this site, and on the operator's definition of night.

cases.mission: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 lander and rover, 69.4 degrees south, landed 23 August 2023; lunar night and expected awakening
cases.terrain: LOLA elevation model of the project (60 m grid at this latitude), terrain horizon out to 300 km, observer 2 m above the surface

published.precision: 0.0001 degree in latitude, 0.01 degree in longitude

published.as_printed: touched down on the Moon on 23 August 2023
September 04, 2023: The lander and rover are in sleep mode.
published.precision: 1 day; ISRO uses Indian Standard Time (UTC+5:30)

published.nature: operator's expectation, not an astronomical event

checks.computed: the first sunrise after the sleep date (first part of the Sun above the terrain horizon, seen from 2 m) must not be later than the end of 22 September 2023 in Indian Standard Time, 2023-09-22T18:30:00 UTC

sunset (last light) and sunrise (first light) over the terrain horizon and on a smooth sphere; elevation of the Sun's centre during 22 September 2023 (IST); days between computed sunrise and 22 September
checks.why_not_judged: ISRO published the state of the spacecraft and an expected wake-up date, not sunset or sunrise times.
